# RTK - Rust Token Killer

**Usage**: Token-optimized CLI proxy (60-90% savings on dev operations)

## Meta Commands (always use rtk directly)

```bash
rtk gain              # Show token savings analytics
rtk gain --history    # Show command usage history with savings
rtk discover          # Analyze Claude Code history for missed opportunities
rtk proxy <cmd>       # Execute raw command without filtering (for debugging)
```

## Installation Verification

```bash
rtk --version         # Should show: rtk X.Y.Z
rtk gain              # Should work (not "command not found")
which rtk             # Verify correct binary
```

⚠️ **Name collision**: If `rtk gain` fails, you may have reachingforthejack/rtk (Rust Type Kit) installed instead.

## Hook-Based Usage

All other commands are automatically rewritten by the Claude Code hook.
Example: `git status` → `rtk git status` (transparent, 0 tokens overhead)

Refer to CLAUDE.md for full command reference.

# Agent guide

Rules for AI agents working in this repo.

## Crates

| Crate | License | Depends on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| callisto-model | MIT | none (external: `michi-graph`, MIT) |
| callisto-manifests | FSL-1.1-MIT | model |
| callisto-graph | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests |
| callisto-cli | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests, graph |
| callisto-fixtures | FSL-1.1-MIT | model (dev-only) |

- `callisto-model` (MIT) must never depend on an FSL crate. It depends on `michi-graph` (MIT, no dependencies of its own) for dependency-graph validation and ordering. `just license-boundary` fails if anything it builds with is FSL.
- Check with `grep -H "^license" crates/*/Cargo.toml` after adding or moving a crate.

## Commands

- Full pipeline: `just ci` (includes the 90% coverage gate). `just test`, `just lint`, `just fmt`.
- Scoped iteration: one `cargo test -p <crate>` or `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings` at a time.
  - Not `moon run <project>:test`: its per-project fan-out serializes on `target/`'s build lock.
  - Never run cargo builds in parallel.
- Changesets: `callisto add --package cargo/callisto-cli:<bump> --summary "..."` (non-interactive). Target `callisto-cli`: its changelog is the one users read. One changeset per user-visible topic, written as the changelog entry: what the user sees now, no internal names or mechanism.
- Never `git checkout -- Cargo.lock` as cleanup. A lockfile diff means investigate, not discard.

## Invariants

1. Safe Rust only: `unsafe_code = "forbid"`.
2. Manifest edits preserve format: `toml_edit` for TOML; JSON keeps key order and fingerprinted indentation. No regex or line edits.
3. File writes go through `callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write`.
4. User-facing errors derive `miette::Diagnostic` with a code and a fix.
5. No emojis in docs or code.
6. No cargo features in shipped crates; behaviour is chosen at runtime (#143). The dev-only `callisto-model/test-util` feature is the exception.
7. No `unwrap()` outside tests (`just lint` denies it). An `expect` names the invariant that makes it unreachable.

## Fixing bugs

- Grep for structurally identical code (same algorithm, other file, ecosystem or mode). A sibling with the same defect is in scope now.
- N copies of one logic: unify to one implementation rather than patching each.
- A deliberately deferred sibling gets an explicit record: changeset note, tracked follow-up or code comment.
- A new shared helper migrates every call site in the same change, or the rest are tracked.

## Specs and plans

- Specs (`spec@1`) live in `docs/specs/`, one per area, current behavior only. Change the spec in the same PR as the behavior. No history, rationale or revision notes.
- This repo's release workflow has no GitHub Environment or reviewer gate and only `execute` gets registry secrets (owner policy, enforced by `.github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh`). Never add one.
- Read `ARCHITECTURE.md` and the matching `docs/architecture/` topic before changing behavior in an area.
- Read `docs/adr/README.md` before changing release flow, Git access, publishing, distribution, platform packages or manifest writes. Reversing an ADR needs a new ADR the owner accepts.
- Plans (`plan@1`) live in `docs/projects/`. Delete a plan once its work ships.
- Code never cites specs: no spec IDs, criterion IDs, section numbers or track names in comments, test names or messages. Describe the behavior instead.
- A requirement the owner didn't state is a judgment call. Get owner confirmation before it gates anything.

## Writing

- Succinct: short sentences, bullets, tables. No backstory, hedging or filler.
- Never hard-wrap Markdown or PR bodies: one line per paragraph.
- Code comments: one short line, only for a non-obvious why. Wrap at 120 columns (`rustfmt.toml`). No history ("used to", "previously"): git records it.
- No claude.ai session links in commits, PRs or files.

# Memory Index

- [Post-0.10.2 Plan](project_post_0_10_2_plan.md) — Open work after the 0.10.2 release lives in .claude/plans/NEXT-WORK.md (local only, never PR it): 12 workstreams, parallel lanes, stacked PRs, owner decisions (D01 blocks MATURIN/OWNER).
- [Prove With the Real Tool](feedback_prove_with_the_real_tool.md) — Fake-tool tests and clean compiles hid the 0.10.1 gh credential regression; reproduce auth/release/registry paths with the real tool, test the failing case first, state what is unproven.
- [Callisto Self-Release Incident — Durable Memory](project_release_self_hosting_incident_2026-09.md) — Claude invented and later misattributed the release approval gate, misunderstood rerun semantics, and repeatedly declared fixes before publication; records non-negotiable policy, verified failures, corrective architecture, and required incident protocol.
- [Hardcoded Values — Proactive Search Required](feedback_hardcoded_values.md) — User repeatedly frustrated by missed hardcoded values; always include a dedicated pass in any audit or fix session.
- [Track 0: gix WASI spike — NO-GO verdict](project_track0_wasi_verdict.md) — mmap ENOSYS in WASI blocks all gix object reads; callisto-moon exec-seam must use warpgate_pdk::exec_command.
- [Publish Pipeline Audit — 38 bugs, fix ordering, semantic coupling map](project_publish_pipeline_audit.md) — Full adversarial audit complete; 5 P0s, 11 P1s, 15+ P2s; three root patterns; phased fix sequence with dependency order.
- [Parallel Fixing Anti-Pattern](feedback_parallel_fixing.md) — Parallel agents for fixes fail on semantically coupled systems even across different files; use parallel for investigation only.
- [Validate Each Fix Individually](feedback_validate_each_fix.md) — Run targeted tests after every individual fix; do not batch changes and rely solely on final CI run.
- Architecture: ARCHITECTURE.md + docs/architecture/ (moved from .claude/semantic-model on 2026-09-25) — read before implementation work.
- [Active Work](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/plans/ACTIVE.md) — Tracks B, E, F (resolve_package_config), G (callisto matrix) all shipped and passing just ci. Pipeline: canon→vector→lambda.
- [Canon Pipeline Scope](feedback_canon_pipeline_scope.md) — Skip canon ceremony for targeted bug fixes with RED tests already written; canon auditor loops infinitely on implementation-detail prose.
- [Workspace Audit 2026-08](project_workspace_audit_2026-08.md) — CLOSED: 8-dimension audit, all critical/high + all 31 medium/low findings re-verified fixed as of 2026-08-27.
- [Found Code Needs Same Rigor](feedback_found_code_needs_same_rigor.md) — Committing pre-existing uncommitted code after only "compiles + existing tests pass" missed a zero-test-coverage regression; found/inherited code needs the same TDD/adversarial rigor as freshly-written code.
- [Manifest Persist Track](project_manifest_persist_track.md) — Both Spec A (mutate/persist split) and Spec B (write-batching) shipped; the apply_version_plan redundant-open/persist audit finding is fully closed.

# Agent guide

Rules for AI agents working in this repo.

## Crates

| Crate | License | Depends on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| callisto-model | MIT | none (external: `michi-graph`, MIT) |
| callisto-manifests | FSL-1.1-MIT | model |
| callisto-graph | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests |
| callisto-cli | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests, graph |
| callisto-fixtures | FSL-1.1-MIT | model (dev-only) |

- `callisto-model` (MIT) must never depend on an FSL crate. It depends on `michi-graph` (MIT, no dependencies of its own) for dependency-graph validation and ordering. `just license-boundary` fails if anything it builds with is FSL.
- Check with `grep -H "^license" crates/*/Cargo.toml` after adding or moving a crate.

## Commands

- Full pipeline: `just ci` (includes the 90% coverage gate). `just test`, `just lint`, `just fmt`.
- Scoped iteration: one `cargo test -p <crate>` or `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings` at a time.
  - Not `moon run <project>:test`: its per-project fan-out serializes on `target/`'s build lock.
  - Never run cargo builds in parallel.
- Changesets: `callisto add --package cargo/callisto-cli:<bump> --summary "..."` (non-interactive). Target `callisto-cli`: its changelog is the one users read. One changeset per user-visible topic, written as the changelog entry: what the user sees now, no internal names or mechanism.
- Never `git checkout -- Cargo.lock` as cleanup. A lockfile diff means investigate, not discard.

## Invariants

1. Safe Rust only: `unsafe_code = "forbid"`.
2. Manifest edits preserve format: `toml_edit` for TOML; JSON keeps key order and fingerprinted indentation. No regex or line edits.
3. File writes go through `callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write`.
4. User-facing errors derive `miette::Diagnostic` with a code and a fix.
5. No emojis in docs or code.
6. No cargo features in shipped crates; behaviour is chosen at runtime (#143). The dev-only `callisto-model/test-util` feature is the exception.
7. No `unwrap()` outside tests (`just lint` denies it). An `expect` names the invariant that makes it unreachable.

## Fixing bugs

- Grep for structurally identical code (same algorithm, other file, ecosystem or mode). A sibling with the same defect is in scope now.
- N copies of one logic: unify to one implementation rather than patching each.
- A deliberately deferred sibling gets an explicit record: changeset note, tracked follow-up or code comment.
- A new shared helper migrates every call site in the same change, or the rest are tracked.

## Specs and plans

- Specs (`spec@1`) live in `docs/specs/`, one per area, current behavior only. Change the spec in the same PR as the behavior. No history, rationale or revision notes.
- This repo's release workflow has no GitHub Environment or reviewer gate and only `execute` gets registry secrets (owner policy, enforced by `.github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh`). Never add one.
- Read `ARCHITECTURE.md` and the matching `docs/architecture/` topic before changing behavior in an area.
- Read `docs/adr/README.md` before changing release flow, Git access, publishing, distribution, platform packages or manifest writes. Reversing an ADR needs a new ADR the owner accepts.
- Plans (`plan@1`) live in `docs/projects/`. Delete a plan once its work ships.
- Code never cites specs: no spec IDs, criterion IDs, section numbers or track names in comments, test names or messages. Describe the behavior instead.
- A requirement the owner didn't state is a judgment call. Get owner confirmation before it gates anything.

## Writing

- Succinct: short sentences, bullets, tables. No backstory, hedging or filler.
- Never hard-wrap Markdown or PR bodies: one line per paragraph.
- Code comments: one short line, only for a non-obvious why. Wrap at 120 columns (`rustfmt.toml`). No history ("used to", "previously"): git records it.
- No claude.ai session links in commits, PRs or files.

# Bug-Hunter Subagent Instructions

You audit any target Rust codebase for latent bugs: silent failures, spec-vs-code drift, ordering/staleness bugs, crash-safety violations, and security/edge-case gaps using Universal Rust Hazard Taxonomies.

## Operational Directives

0. **Read-only**: Investigate and report; do not edit files or run mutating commands unless the task explicitly asks for a fix. Read `../callisto-findings/FINDINGS.md` (if present) — skip re-reporting anything already logged as `CONFIRMED`. This ledger lives outside the repo, deliberately — it names unfixed defects and must never be committed here (this repo is public).
1. **Trace end-to-end**: Don't stop at interface boundaries — follow data from CLI/API inputs through domain models, graph algorithms, manifest editors, down to disk I/O.
2. **Hazard-Taxonomy Partitioning**: Execute audits focused on specific Hazard Categories (1. Discarded Parameters, 2. Fixpoint Staleness, 3. Spec Drift, 4. Silent Fallbacks, 5. Boundary Edge Cases, 6. Crash-Safety & Subprocesses) across the entire target workspace.
3. **Verify before reporting**: Try to disprove the finding first (check for a guard you may have missed). Give a concrete failing scenario (specific input, state, or flag). Mark `CONFIRMED` (path fully traced) or `PLAUSIBLE` (strong signal, not fully traced).
4. **Structured Reporting**: Use the format in `../skills/bug-hunter/SKILL.md` — Status, Location (`file:line`), Classification, Root Cause, Failing Scenario, Severity, Verification Strategy.
5. **Sibling sweep, not single hit**: When a confirmed defect is one instance of a structurally repeated pattern (same algorithm reimplemented per ecosystem/mode/branch), grep for every other instance before reporting it as one finding. List all sibling locations in the same finding and note whether the fix should be "patch each copy" or "unify into one implementation" — the latter is preferred whenever N>1 copies exist. A finding that names only the first instance you tripped over, when siblings exist, is an incomplete finding.

4. **Silent Fallbacks & Falsified Defaults**: Catch-all `unwrap_or` defaults hiding invalid state, swallowed I/O errors.
5. **Boundary Inputs & Format Edge Cases**: UTF-8 BOM (`\u{FEFF}`), CRLF line endings, unicode paths, detached HEAD Git states.
6. **Crash-Safety & Subprocess Security**: Atomic writes missing `.flush()` or `.sync_all()`, subprocess argument ordering.

---

## The 6 Architectural Code Smells & Ripgrep Sweeps

1. **Raw String Identity Smell**: `entry.name == pkg.id.to_string()` (Mismatched bare vs prefixed string comparison).
2. **Un-Transactional Disk Mutation Smell**: Step-by-step file edits without atomic batch rollback.

This ledger lives outside the repo, deliberately — it names unfixed defects and must never be committed here (this repo is public).
15	1. **Trace end-to-end**: Don't stop at interface boundaries — follow data from CLI/API inputs through domain models, graph algorithms, manifest editors, down to disk I/O.

19	5. **Sibling sweep, not single hit**: When a confirmed defect is one instance of a structurally repeated pattern (same algorithm reimplemented per ecosystem/mode/branch), grep for every other instance before reporting it as one finding. List all sibling locations in the same finding and note whether the fix should be "patch each copy" or "unify into one implementation" — the latter is preferred whenever N>1 copies exist. A finding that names only the first instance you tripped over, when siblings exist, is an incomplete finding.

2	name: bug-hunter
3	description: >-
4	  Universal, repo-agnostic Rust bug hunting framework. Finds silent failures, spec-vs-code drift, ordering/staleness bugs, crash-safety violations, and edge cases across any Rust codebase using Hazard-Taxonomy Partitioning.
5	---
6	
7	# Universal Rust Bug-Hunter Skill
8	
9	## Goal
10	
11	Find real bugs before they ship in any Rust repository (monorepos, CLI engines, libraries, polyglot WASM plugins): silent failures, spec-vs-code drift, data corruption, ordering staleness, crash-safety violations, and edge cases that break production.
12	
13	This skill is **Rigid**: follow it exactly across any Rust workspace.
14	
15	## The Law
16	
17	> NO FINDING MARKED `CONFIRMED` WITHOUT AN END-TO-END TRACE. NO FIX MARKED DONE WITHOUT A TEST THAT FAILED BEFORE THE FIX AND PASSES AFTER, RUN IN THIS SESSION.
18	
19	## Core Rules
20	
21	- **Verify by Tracing**: Don't trust a comment, docstring, passing test, or a prior audit's "FIXED" label. Trace the code execution path yourself.
22	- **Hazard-Taxonomy Partitioning**: When executing multi-agent bug hunts, DO NOT partition subagents by directory or crate names. ALWAYS partition subagents by **Hazard Taxonomy** or **Code Smell Sweep** across the entire workspace.
23	- **Strict Invariants**: Prioritize data integrity, crash-safety, error propagation, and security bugs over style or refactoring.
24	- **Read-Only Investigation**: Investigate and report findings first. Do not mutate files unless explicitly requested to apply fixes.
25	
26	---
27	
28	## The 6 Universal Rust Hazard Taxonomies
29	
30	1. **Discarded Data & Unused CLI / Struct Parameters**: Leading-underscore parameters (`_opts`, `_config`), unused Clap CLI flags.
31	2. **Ordering, Mutability & Fixpoint Staleness**: First-write-wins vs max-value-wins, graph solver loops missing re-enqueueing logic.
32	3. **Spec-vs-Code Compliance Drift**: Requirements in design docs/specs missing enforcement logic in functions.
33	4. **Silent Fallbacks & Falsified Defaults**: Catch-all `unwrap_or` defaults hiding invalid state, swallowed I/O errors.
34	5. **Boundary Inputs & Format Edge Cases**: UTF-8 BOM (`\u{FEFF}`), CRLF line endings, unicode paths, detached HEAD Git states.
35	6. **Crash-Safety & Subprocess Security**: Atomic writes missing `.flush()` or `.sync_all()`, subprocess argument ordering.
36	
37	---
38	
39	## The 6 Architectural Code Smells & Ripgrep Sweeps
40	
41	1. **Raw String Identity Smell**: `entry.name == pkg.id.to_string()` (Mismatched bare vs prefixed string comparison).
42	2. **Un-Transactional Disk Mutation Smell**: Step-by-step file edits without atomic batch rollback.
43	3. **Lossy Serde / CST Formatting Smell**: Replacing TOML/JSON nodes without preserving `.decor()` or line endings.
44	4. **Un-Fsynced Directory Metadata Smell**: `create_dir_all` or `atomic_write` missing parent directory `sync_all()`.
45	5. **Scopeless Fallback & Unbounded Traversal Smell**: Unbounded `revwalk` commit loops or catch-all `unwrap_or_else` defaults.
46	6. **Hardcoded Constant Dummy Smell**: Inserting placeholder strings (`"Release update"`, `"changeset.md"`) masking user metadata.
47

51	
52	When auditing multi-crate workspaces, map recurring defects directly to 7 Centralized Rust Traits:
53	1. `PackageIdentityResolver`: Cross-ecosystem package matching and bare name resolution.
54	2. `VersionSpecRenderer`: Format & precision-preserving version requirement rendering.
55	3. `ChangesetStorage`: Crash-safe, transactional disk engine with parent directory fsync.
56	4. `CstManifestEditor`: CST format-preserving manifest modification (`toml_edit` and `serde_json`).
57	5. `GitVcsProvider`: Safe Git tags, shallow checkout handling, and bounded revwalk.
58	6. `CascadeSolver`: Fixpoint dependency graph solver & convergence tracking.
59	7. `ReportPresenter`: Unified text & JSON report renderer with rich `miette` diagnostic cards.

Callisto Architecture

Crate map, data flow, and the invariants every change must preserve.

--- ## Invariants 1. **Safe Rust only.** `unsafe_code = "forbid"` workspace-wide. 2. **License boundary.** `callisto-model` is MIT and must never depend on an FSL-1.1-MIT crate. Every other crate is FSL-1.1-MIT. Check with `grep -H "^license" crates/*/Cargo.toml`. 3. **Format-preserving manifest edits.** `Cargo.toml` goes through `toml_edit`'s CST; `package.json` is fingerprinted for indent style and line endings before a `serde_json` (`preserve_order`) round trip. No regex or line-based edits to manifests. 4. **One file-write primitive, capability-gated.** `callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write` (`NamedTempFile` in the target's own directory, `fsync`, `persist` via `fs::rename`, then `fsync` the parent directory, and its parent when the call created it; a failed sync is returned unless the filesystem cannot sync a directory) is the only way file content is written; deletions and directory creation use `std::fs`. It takes `&ApplyPermit`, a token with a private field that only `ApplyPermit::granted_unless_dry_run(dry_run)` can construct, returning `None` on a dry run. A write path that forgets to check `--dry-run` has no permit to pass and fails to compile. 5. **System Git only.** All VCS reads and writes shell out to the user's `git` binary (`callisto_model::vcs`), so Callisto sees exactly the repository, config, and identity Git itself does. No embedded Git implementation. 6. **Versioning.** The four published crates version in lockstep (one fixed group). Only `callisto-cli`, its command-line interface and its JSON reports are a compatibility surface; `callisto-model`, `callisto-manifests` and `callisto-graph` are internal and may change in any release. 7. **User-facing errors are diagnosable.** Every error surfaced to a user derives `miette::Diagnostic` with a stable code and, where the fix isn't obvious from the message, `help` text. A wrapper around another crate's error (for example `GraphError::Config`) is `#[diagnostic(transparent)]` and declares no code of its own, so the inner code reaches the user. Full list: [`docs/errors.md`](docs/errors.md). Design decisions, with the options they rejected and why: [`docs/adr/README.md`](docs/adr/README.md). ## Crate map ``` Layer 1 (leaf) callisto-model Layer 2 (I/O) callisto-manifests Layer 3 (engine) callisto-graph Layer 4 (surface) callisto-cli Dev-only callisto-fixtures ``` | Crate | License | Depends on | Purpose | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | [`callisto-model`](crates/callisto-model) | MIT | none (external: `michi-graph`) | Domain primitives (`PackageId`, `Version`, `Severity`, `Changeset`, `PreState`), `atomic_write`, `ApplyPermit`, the `CommandRunner`/`DependencyResolver` trait seams; `format`: `.changeset/*.md` and `pre.json` parser/writer; `vcs`: `GitAccess`, every Git operation as a subprocess through `CommandRunner` | | [`callisto-manifests`](crates/callisto-manifests) | FSL-1.1-MIT | model | `Manifest` trait; format-preserving Cargo/npm/PyPI manifest editors | | [`callisto-graph`](crates/callisto-graph) | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests | Dependency graph, cascade engine, version planning, release execution; `conventional`: Conventional Commit parsing and bump inference; `changelog`: Markdown changelog rendering | | [`callisto-cli`](crates/callisto-cli) | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests, graph | `clap` CLI surface, `miette` diagnostic rendering | | [`callisto-fixtures`](crates/callisto-fixtures) | FSL-1.1-MIT | model (dev-only) | Multi-ecosystem test corpus and in-memory test doubles | Dependencies only point down the layers (`cli` → `graph` → `manifests` → `model`). Nothing in Layer 1–3 depends on `callisto-cli`. ## Data flow ``` Workspace::load config::load -> config::resolve callisto.toml -> ResolvedConfig ManifestWalkResolver::build discover (ProjectLocator), read manifests (Manifest), assign ids, attach platform packages, apply per-package config GroupTable::resolve bind [[fixed-group]] / [[linked-group]] members plan_version -> VersionPlan (in memory) aggregate changesets + opt-in commit inference -> severity per package run_cascade dependents (runtime, build, optional, peer; never dev), groups, pre mode -> target version per package, with its reasons version --emit-decision derives and validates the decision in memory, before apply apply_version_plan (needs ApplyPermit) CST edits -> atomic_write, changelogs consume changesets -> native lock refresh -> git staging version --emit-decision writes the decision file after successful apply release decision -> intent -> envelope -> execute_release -> receipt per operation observe provider -> adopt, or perform and confirm ``` Package ordering, cycle reports and release-operation readiness all run on `michi-graph` (validation reports every problem at once; edge kinds are chosen per validation). Git access goes through `GitAccess` (`callisto_model::vcs`). Depth: - [`docs/architecture/identity.md`](docs/architecture/identity.md): package ids, bare-name matching, config rule specificity, workspace loading, platform packages. - [`docs/architecture/versioning.md`](docs/architecture/versioning.md): plan and apply, file-level idempotence and interrupted-command limits. - [`docs/architecture/release.md`](docs/architecture/release.md): release terms, the two routes, run envelope, observation and proof tokens, the transition table, verification tiers. - [`docs/architecture/wire-compat.md`](docs/architecture/wire-compat.md): the version each release document writes and reads, what a reader does with another, and the known gaps. ## Extension seams Four traits decouple the engine from platform I/O (`callisto-model::exec`, `callisto-model::discovery`, `callisto-manifests`, `callisto-graph::locate`): - `ProjectLocator` — enumerates workspace project roots. - `CommandRunner` — runs a subprocess. `run_with_timeout`'s default implementation ignores the timeout; the CLI's runner enforces it, so a hung publish command cannot block forever. - `Manifest` — per-ecosystem read/write. Mutations only touch the in-memory CST; nothing reaches disk until `persist(&ApplyPermit)`, so one open manifest can take several mutations before one write. - `DependencyResolver` — supplies graph nodes and edges; `ManifestWalkResolver` is the only current implementation. ## Current boundaries and planned changes `PackageId` is a flexible selector/display form; `PackageKey` is a directory locator; `ReleasePackageId` is a canonical ecosystem-qualified distribution identity. A directory can own several canonical manifests, but the current package model requires one version grammar. Registry version observations do not establish a complete Python file set or identical package bytes. Remaining v1 work is in [`docs/projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md`](docs/projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md). The canonical-identity and polyglot model is in [`docs/architecture/polyglot-v1.md`](docs/architecture/polyglot-v1.md); only the parts it marks as design are not implemented, and none is an extension seam. The existing dependency graph and release-operation DAG remain the basis of the plan. ## Not covered here - Release lifecycle, CI plan/build/execute, recovery: [`docs/releasing.md`](docs/releasing.md). - Registry authentication: [`docs/publishing.md`](docs/publishing.md). - `callisto.toml` keys: [`docs/config.md`](docs/config.md). - Diagnostic codes: [`docs/errors.md`](docs/errors.md). - Behavior, including `callisto matrix`: [`docs/specs/`](docs/specs/INDEX.md). # Plan and apply How `callisto version` turns changesets into file edits, and where interrupted-command recovery stops. Behavior: [`docs/specs/versioning.json`](../specs/versioning.json). Write mechanics: [ADR 8](../adr/0008-format-preserving-writes-gated-by-apply-permit.md). The emitted decision: [ADR 2](../adr/0002-committed-decision-is-release-authority.md). ## Two phases | Phase | Entry point | Touches disk | | --- | --- | --- | | Plan | `commands::plan_version` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs`) returns a `VersionPlan` | No | | Apply | `apply_version_plan` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs`) | Yes; takes `&ApplyPermit` | - `VersionPlan` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/plan.rs`) is the whole change: bumps, dependency spec rewrites, platform manifest writes, owner `optionalDependencies` pins, changelog sections, consumed changesets, `pre.json` updates and diagnostics. It is in memory only (no `Serialize`). - `plan_version` is shared: `version`, `status`, `compose-pr-body` and `release plan --package` all compute the same plan. - A dry run never gets a permit, so it reports the plan and never calls apply. - `snapshot` applies with `ApplyOptions::transient`: manifests are written, while changelogs, changeset deletion and git staging are skipped. ## Idempotent apply A crash can stop apply after some files are written. Applying the same in-memory plan again is file-level idempotent; a fresh command does not retain that plan. - Each `PlannedBump` carries `from` and `to`. Before writing a manifest (or a platform manifest), apply reads its current version: `from` means write, `to` means already done, anything else is `UnexpectedManifestVersion`. - A manifest already at `to` is still staged: the crashed run may have written it without `git add`. - Apply refreshes affected lockfiles and stages generated version state before consuming changesets or exiting `pre.json`. It stages input deletions with `git rm --cached --ignore-unmatch` before removing the files from disk, so a failed index update leaves the inputs available for recovery. A fresh command does not retain the in-memory plan and can refuse already-stable staged outputs; E121 directs the user to inspect both diffs and finish consuming retained inputs only when the staged outputs are verified. Automatic replay is not guaranteed. - `[workspace.package]` version writes (`VersionWriteTarget::CargoWorkspacePackage`) have no `from`/`to` precondition; they are written unconditionally. - `ApplyOutcome::staged` lists every path apply staged. ## Command boundary and known gaps `version --emit-decision` derives and validates the decision before writes, applies the plan, and writes the decision only after apply succeeds. The decision file is not wrapped in the stdout report envelope. Outside `mode: pre`, `check_partial_run` refuses with E121 when a canonical manifest's effective version differs from `HEAD` while a changeset remains in `HEAD` or in the working tree (including untracked files), or when a canonical manifest with an effective staged version change is present in the index. Staged metadata-only edits are allowed. During `mode: exit`, prerelease versions awaiting stable finalization remain eligible, but changed stable versions are not exempt from the retry guard. It does not restore a lost plan. Apply retains changesets and pre-state deletion inputs until lock refresh and staging of generated state succeed, then stages their removal before unlinking them from disk. Crate map, data flow, and the invariants every change must preserve.

--- ## Invariants 1. **Safe Rust only.** `unsafe_code = "forbid"` workspace-wide. 2. **License boundary.** `callisto-model` is MIT and must never depend on an FSL-1.1-MIT crate. Every other crate is FSL-1.1-MIT. Check with `grep -H "^license" crates/*/Cargo.toml`. 3. **Format-preserving manifest edits.** `Cargo.toml` goes through `toml_edit`'s CST; `package.json` is fingerprinted for indent style and line endings before a `serde_json` (`preserve_order`) round trip. No regex or line-based edits to manifests. 4. **One file-write primitive, capability-gated.** `callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write` (`NamedTempFile` in the target's own directory, `fsync`, `persist` via `fs::rename`, then `fsync` the parent directory, and its parent when the call created it; a failed sync is returned unless the filesystem cannot sync a directory) is the only way file content is written; deletions and directory creation use `std::fs`. It takes `&ApplyPermit`, a token with a private field that only `ApplyPermit::granted_unless_dry_run(dry_run)` can construct, returning `None` on a dry run. A write path that forgets to check `--dry-run` has no permit to pass and fails to compile. 5. **System Git only.** All VCS reads and writes shell out to the user's `git` binary (`callisto_model::vcs`), so Callisto sees exactly the repository, config, and identity Git itself does. No embedded Git implementation. 6. **Versioning.** The four published crates version in lockstep (one fixed group). Only `callisto-cli`, its command-line interface and its JSON reports are a compatibility surface; `callisto-model`, `callisto-manifests` and `callisto-graph` are internal and may change in any release. 7. **User-facing errors are diagnosable.** Every error surfaced to a user derives `miette::Diagnostic` with a stable code and, where the fix isn't obvious from the message, `help` text. A wrapper around another crate's error (for example `GraphError::Config`) is `#[diagnostic(transparent)]` and declares no code of its own, so the inner code reaches the user. input.message:
Adversarial review: versioning and manifest-editing correctness. Callisto v0.14.2, read-only on the repo. `$TMPDIR` resolved to `/tmp/claude-501`, so my scratch repos are under `/tmp/claude-501/adv-version-44777/r1` to `r17`.

Method: the prebuilt binary run with `--no-refresh-lockfiles` on those repos, plus reading the code. Git is blocked by the worktree guard, so I created the repos from a Python helper that shells out to `/usr/bin/git`.

`../callisto-findings/FINDINGS.md` does not exist, so nothing was filtered against it. Nothing was written into the repo.

All paths below are relative to `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/smoke-main`. REPRODUCED means I ran it and saw the output. READ means traced in code only.

## Findings, ranked

### 1. HIGH: a changeset with one unresolved entry re-bumps its resolved packages on every run (REPRODUCED)
- **Location:** `crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs:316`, `:392` and `:413`.
- **Cause:** an entry that does not resolve sets `has_unresolved`, so the changeset is not added to `consumed`. The resolved entries still seed severities and write changelog input.
- **Trigger:** `.changeset/x.md` containing `core: minor` and `ghost: patch`. Typos, a removed package, a PyPI name written normalised (`my-pkg-core` for `My_Pkg.core`) and YAML single-quoted names (`'core': major`) all do the same. A `'core': major` entry is silently dropped, so the package gets the wrong bump.
- **Output:**
  - Run 1 gives `core 1.0.0 -> 1.1.0` with exit 0 and only a warning.
  - After committing, run 2 gives `core 1.1.0 -> 1.2.0`, and `CHANGELOG.md` gets a second `## 1.2.0 - feat`.
  - In pre mode the counter would advance each run.
- **Fix direction:** make an unresolved entry a hard error for the whole run. Or consume the changeset and strip only the unresolved entries. Never apply a changeset that is then kept.

### 2. MEDIUM-HIGH: peer ranges are ratcheted to the latest patch on any co-release (REPRODUCED)
- **Location:** `crates/callisto-graph/src/cascade.rs:443-490` (floor-raise loop; it skips only Dev edges). VER-CAS-06 states this behaviour for peers, so it is spec-conformant.
- **Trigger:** npm workspace where `x` has `peerDependencies: {"core": "^1.0.0"}` and one changeset names `core: patch` and `x: patch`.
- **Output:** `x/package.json` becomes `"core": "^1.4.1"` (with `core` going 1.4.0 to 1.4.1). Consumers on core 1.4.0 then get an ERESOLVE or peer conflict.
- **Fix direction:** exclude `Peer` from the co-release floor raise. Rewrite peers only when the range no longer covers the new version.

### 3. MEDIUM: space-separated and hyphen npm ranges are silently ignored, contradicting the spec (REPRODUCED)
- **Location:** `crates/callisto-model/src/version.rs:217-246` (the npm branch splits only on `||`, then hands each part to the `semver` crate, which wants commas). Failures become `DepSpec::Opaque` in `crates/callisto-manifests/src/npm.rs:parse_npm_spec_str`. Coverage is then Unknown, treated as Covers, with no diagnostic (`crates/callisto-graph/src/cascade.rs:101` and `:249`).
- **Trigger:** `"core": ">=1.0.0 <2.0.0"` or `"core": "1.0.0 - 1.9.9"` while `core` goes to 2.0.0.
- **Output:** the plan shows only `core` bumped. The dependent is left unchanged and unbumped, with no E319 and no warning.
- **Why it matters:** VER-CAS-06 names "an npm range with spaces ... a hyphen" as E319. Only `||` ranges (`^1.0.0 || ^0.9.0`) give E319.
- **Fix direction:** parse npm comparator sets natively. At minimum, emit `RangeNotRoundTrippable` or E319 for an unparsable npm range on a workspace edge.

### 4. MEDIUM: workspace-root `Cargo.toml` loses BOM and CRLF on every write (REPRODUCED)
- **Location:** `crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs:939-950` (`read_from` does not detect a fingerprint) and `:1074-1077` (`persist` writes `document.to_string()`). Member manifests use `FormatFingerprint`; this path does not.
- **Trigger:** root `Cargo.toml` with BOM and CRLF, plus a `[workspace.dependencies]` entry that needs a rewrite.
- **Output:** the file becomes pure LF with no BOM, a whole-file diff. The member `Cargo.toml` files kept CRLF and BOM correctly. This is the "F4" bug in `common.rs` fixed for members but not for the resolver.
- **Fix direction:** route `WorkspaceCargoResolver` through `FormatFingerprint::detect` and `apply`, as `CargoToml` does.

### 5. MEDIUM: BOM'd changelog gets a duplicate H1 and a mid-file BOM (REPRODUCED)
- **Location:** `crates/callisto-graph/src/changelog/write.rs:61-70`. `strip_prefix("# {name}\n")` fails when the file starts with U+FEFF, so it takes the "no matching H1" branch.
- **Trigger:** `CHANGELOG.md` = BOM + `# p\r\n\r\n## 1.0.0 ...` then a release.
- **Output:** the new file is `# p ## 1.1.0 ...` followed by `<BOM># p ## 1.0.0 ...`.
- **Fix direction:** strip and remember the BOM in `prepend`, as the manifest code does. Also match an existing H1 case-insensitively or by shape, so renames do not duplicate it.

### 6. MEDIUM: release notes are cut off at the first indented `# ` line in a summary (READ, with the generated input reproduced)
- **Location:** `crates/callisto-graph/src/changelog/write.rs:119` uses `trimmed = line.trim_start()`, then `starts_with("## ") || starts_with("# ")`. It is used by `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/notes.rs:29`.
- **Trigger:** a changeset summary containing a fenced code block with a `# comment` line. `render_section` indents continuation lines by two spaces, so the line is written as `  # install it`.
- **Output:** the changelog is written correctly, but `find_section` ends the section there. The GitHub release body ends with an unterminated code fence.
- **Related defect:** the idempotence guard at `write.rs:53` compares `l.trim() == "## X"`, so an indented line in an old bullet can suppress a new section.
- **Fix direction:** end a section only on an unindented heading line.

### 7. MEDIUM: `package.json` rewrite is lossy for numbers and expands inline structures (REPRODUCED)
- **Location:** `crates/callisto-manifests/src/npm.rs:116-135` (`format_json_pretty`) and `:289` (`persist`). It re-serialises the whole document through `serde_json`.
- **Output** for a hand-formatted file:
  - `12345678901234567890123` becomes `1.2345678901234568e+22`.
  - `1.10` becomes `1.1`, and `1e3` becomes `1000.0`.
  - `"files": ["dist","src"]` becomes a multi-line array.
  - `é` is un-escaped, and `\/` becomes `/`.
- **Contradiction:** this conflicts with ARCHITECTURE invariant 3 and the "never corrupt" goal. Only `indent`, CRLF, BOM and the trailing newline are preserved.
- **Fix direction:** patch the `"version"` and dependency string spans in place. Or use a lossless JSON CST, or at least `arbitrary_precision` plus preserved raw arrays.

### 8. MEDIUM: one version-less or dynamic-version member aborts the entire `version` run (REPRODUCED)
- **Trigger:** a Cargo member with `publish = false` and no `version` (xtask-style, which Cargo allows). A pyproject with `dynamic = ["version"]` (hatch-vcs, setuptools-scm) behaves the same.
- **Output:** E013 for the whole workspace, even though that member is not being released. The help text only suggests excluding it from discovery.
- **Location:** E013 raised from `current_version` in `crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs` and `python.rs`.
- **Fix direction:** skip non-publishable or dynamic-version members with a warning unless they are named by a changeset or edge.

### 9. MEDIUM: Python `~=` and Poetry rewrites change compatibility precision (REPRODUCED)
- **Location:** `crates/callisto-manifests/src/python.rs:772-810` (`rewrite_single`, `render_target` always emit `major.minor.patch`).
- **Trigger:** `Core[extra] ~= 1.2` with `core` going to 2.0.0.
- **Output:** the spec becomes `Core[extra]~=2.0.0`. That is narrower: `~=1.2` allowed 1.x, `~=2.0.0` allows only 2.0.x. A consumer wanting core 2.1 hits a resolver conflict. Cargo and npm keep precision; PEP 440 does not.
- **Fix direction:** keep the original component count for `~=`.

### 10. LOW-MEDIUM: Poetry dependency rewrites drop trailing comments (REPRODUCED)
- **Location:** `crates/callisto-manifests/src/python.rs:600` (`fields.insert("version", value(...))`) and `:603` (`table.insert(name, ...)`). Neither carries over decor, unlike `cargo::set_dependency_version`.
- **Trigger:** `core = "^1.2"  # keep poetry`, and `version = "~1.2.3"  # c2` under `[tool.poetry.dependencies.core]`.
- **Output:** both comments are lost. PEP 621 arrays keep theirs via `Array::replace`. The doc comment on `PyprojectToml` claims "100% CST comment preservation".
- **Fix direction:** copy `decor()` as `set_scalar_preserving_decor` does.

### 11. LOW-MEDIUM: apply is not transactional, and preflight does not dry-run the edits (REPRODUCED)
- **Location:** `crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs` (write loop) and `crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs:560-575` (`write_version` needs `package` to be a block table).
- **Trigger:** `a` (normal) and `b` with `package = { name = "b", version = "1.0.0" }`, both named in one changeset.
- **Output:** `a/Cargo.toml` is already rewritten to 1.1.0 when `b` fails with E013. Nothing is staged. The next run then hits E121 because the tree differs from HEAD.
- **Related:** the same shape applies to an E208 lockfile-refresh failure after writes. That one is documented in `docs/architecture/versioning.md`.
- **Fix direction:** open every manifest and apply all mutations in memory before the first persist (a two-phase apply).

### 12. LOW: snapshot tag validation (REPRODUCED)
- **Trigger:** `snapshot --tag feat/x_y`, `a b`, `..` or `é`.
- **Output:** E038 "internal error computing bumped version" instead of a usage error. `--tag x+y` is accepted for SemVer as `0.0.0-x+y-<sha>`, which puts the sha in build metadata. Two snapshots with the same tag then compare equal.
- **Fix direction:** validate the tag up front against the native grammar and map it to a user-facing diagnostic.

## Smaller notes (not ranked)
- A changeset naming `core` and `cargo/core` produces a duplicated changelog bullet. The max severity is correct.
- Blank continuation lines in changelog bullets carry two trailing spaces (`render.rs` `replace('\n', "\n  ")`).
- A pnpm `catalog:` spec is never rewritten, and an unmatched catalog entry is only warned about. This is by spec, but a major bump leaves the catalog pinned to the old major.
- Dead path: `VersionWriteTarget::CargoWorkspacePackage` is never produced by the planner (only tests), so `[workspace.package] version` is never written. A member with `version.workspace = true` is pinned to a literal on bump, which looks intended.

## Done well
- **Cargo.toml edits:** the CST edits preserve comments, inline tables, dotted keys (`core.version = ...`), renamed `package =` deps, target-specific and build/dev tables, and CRLF and BOM on members. Duplicate keys are rejected on parse.
- **Cargo workspace inheritance:** `workspace = true` deps are rewritten once in the root `[workspace.dependencies]`, including when the root is itself a package (r15).
- **Cascade:** it converged on peer cycles, with escalation and fixed-group handling (r7). A rewrite that would still exclude the new version is declined rather than written, and bare-caret coverage of `0.x` and prereleases is correct. Pre-mode lifecycle worked end to end: `beta.0`, `beta.1`, `pre exit` stabilises dependents, and floors are raised (r6).
- **Write primitive:** `callisto_model::atomic_write` fsyncs the file and the parent, keeps the file mode, and is gated by `ApplyPermit`. The `check_partial_run` E121 guard stops stacked double bumps after an interrupted run. The per-file `from`/`to` precondition (`write_version_guarded`) makes replay safe.
- **Changeset parser:** strict and well-specified. It handles BOM, CRLF and CR, quoted names containing `:`, duplicate detection with line numbers, and an empty summary rejection. Hostile summaries (`---`, headings, HTML) are indented into a bullet and cannot create a top-level changelog heading.

Adversarial review: versioning and manifest-editing correctness. Callisto v0.14.2, read-only on the repo. `$TMPDIR` resolved to `/tmp/claude-501`, so my scratch repos are under `/tmp/claude-501/adv-version-44777/r1` to `r17`.

Method: the prebuilt binary run with `--no-refresh-lockfiles` on those repos, plus reading the code. Git is blocked by the worktree guard, so I created the repos from a Python helper that shells out to `/usr/bin/git`.

`../callisto-findings/FINDINGS.md` does not exist, so nothing was filtered against it. Nothing was written into the repo.

All paths below are relative to `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/smoke-main`. REPRODUCED means I ran it and saw the output. READ means traced in code only.

## Findings, ranked

### 1. HIGH: a changeset with one unresolved entry re-bumps its resolved packages on every run (REPRODUCED)
- **Location:** `crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs:316`, `:392` and `:413`.
- **Cause:** an entry that does not resolve sets `has_unresolved`, so the changeset is not added to `consumed`. The resolved entries still seed severities and write changelog input.
- **Trigger:** `.changeset/x.md` containing `core: minor` and `ghost: patch`. Typos, a removed package, a PyPI name written normalised (`my-pkg-core` for `My_Pkg.core`) and YAML single-quoted names (`'core': major`) all do the same. A `'core': major` entry is silently dropped, so the package gets the wrong bump.
- **Output:**
  - Run 1 gives `core 1.0.0 -> 1.1.0` with exit 0 and only a warning.
  - After committing, run 2 gives `core 1.1.0 -> 1.2.0`, and `CHANGELOG.md` gets a second `## 1.2.0 - feat`.
  - In pre mode the counter would advance each run.
- **Fix direction:** make an unresolved entry a hard error for the whole run. Or consume the changeset and strip only the unresolved entries. Never apply a changeset that is then kept.

### 2. MEDIUM-HIGH: peer ranges are ratcheted to the latest patch on any co-release (REPRODUCED)
- **Location:** `crates/callisto-graph/src/cascade.rs:443-490` (floor-raise loop; it skips only Dev edges). VER-CAS-06 states this behaviour for peers, so it is spec-conformant.
- **Trigger:** npm workspace where `x` has `peerDependencies: {"core": "^1.0.0"}` and one changeset names `core: patch` and `x: patch`.
- **Output:** `x/package.json` becomes `"core": "^1.4.1"` (with `core` going 1.4.0 to 1.4.1). Consumers on core 1.4.0 then get an ERESOLVE or peer conflict.
- **Fix direction:** exclude `Peer` from the co-release floor raise. Rewrite peers only when the range no longer covers the new version.

### 3. MEDIUM: space-separated and hyphen npm ranges are silently ignored, contradicting the spec (REPRODUCED)
- **Location:** `crates/callisto-model/src/version.rs:217-246` (the npm branch splits only on `||`, then hands each part to the `semver` crate, which wants commas). Failures become `DepSpec::Opaque` in `crates/callisto-manifests/src/npm.rs:parse_npm_spec_str`. Coverage is then Unknown, treated as Covers, with no diagnostic (`crates/callisto-graph/src/cascade.rs:101` and `:249`).
- **Trigger:** `"core": ">=1.0.0 <2.0.0"` or `"core": "1.0.0 - 1.9.9"` while `core` goes to 2.0.0.
- **Output:** the plan shows only `core` bumped. The dependent is left unchanged and unbumped, with no E319 and no warning.
- **Why it matters:** VER-CAS-06 names "an npm range with spaces ... a hyphen" as E319. Only `||` ranges (`^1.0.0 || ^0.9.0`) give E319.
- **Fix direction:** parse npm comparator sets natively. At minimum, emit `RangeNotRoundTrippable` or E319 for an unparsable npm range on a workspace edge.

### 4. MEDIUM: workspace-root `Cargo.toml` loses BOM and CRLF on every write (REPRODUCED)
- **Location:** `crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs:939-950` (`read_from` does not detect a fingerprint) and `:1074-1077` (`persist` writes `document.to_string()`). Member manifests use `FormatFingerprint`; this path does not.
- **Trigger:** root `Cargo.toml` with BOM and CRLF, plus a `[workspace.dependencies]` entry that needs a rewrite.
- **Output:** the file becomes pure LF with no BOM, a whole-file diff. The member `Cargo.toml` files kept CRLF and BOM correctly. This is the "F4" bug in `common.rs` fixed for members but not for the resolver.
- **Fix direction:** route `WorkspaceCargoResolver` through `FormatFingerprint::detect` and `apply`, as `CargoToml` does.

### 5. MEDIUM: BOM'd changelog gets a duplicate H1 and a mid-file BOM (REPRODUCED)
- **Location:** `crates/callisto-graph/src/changelog/write.rs:61-70`. `strip_prefix("# {name}\n")` fails when the file starts with U+FEFF, so it takes the "no matching H1" branch.
- **Trigger:** `CHANGELOG.md` = BOM + `# p\r\n\r\n## 1.0.0 ...` then a release.
- **Output:** the new file is `# p ## 1.1.0 ...` followed by `<BOM># p ## 1.0.0 ...`.
- **Fix direction:** strip and remember the BOM in `prepend`, as the manifest code does. Also match an existing H1 case-insensitively or by shape, so renames do not duplicate it.

### 6. MEDIUM: release notes are cut off at the first indented `# ` line in a summary (READ, with the generated input reproduced)
- **Location:** `crates/callisto-graph/src/changelog/write.rs:119` uses `trimmed = line.trim_start()`, then `starts_with("## ") || starts_with("# ")`. It is used by `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/notes.rs:29`.
- **Trigger:** a changeset summary containing a fenced code block with a `# comment` line. `render_section` indents continuation lines by two spaces, so the line is written as `  # install it`.
- **Output:** the changelog is written correctly, but `find_section` ends the section there. The GitHub release body ends with an unterminated code fence.
- **Related defect:** the idempotence guard at `write.rs:53` compares `l.trim() == "## X"`, so an indented line in an old bullet can suppress a new section.
- **Fix direction:** end a section only on an unindented heading line.

### 7. MEDIUM: `package.json` rewrite is lossy for numbers and expands inline structures (REPRODUCED)
- **Location:** `crates/callisto-manifests/src/npm.rs:116-135` (`format_json_pretty`) and `:289` (`persist`). It re-serialises the whole document through `serde_json`.
- **Output** for a hand-formatted file:
  - `12345678901234567890123` becomes `1.2345678901234568e+22`.
  - `1.10` becomes `1.1`, and `1e3` becomes `1000.0`.
  - `"files": ["dist","src"]` becomes a multi-line array.
  - `\u00e9` is un-escaped, and `\/` becomes `/`.
- **Contradiction:** this conflicts with ARCHITECTURE invariant 3 and the "never corrupt" goal. Only `indent`, CRLF, BOM and the trailing newline are preserved.
- **Fix direction:** patch the `"version"` and dependency string spans in place. Or use a lossless JSON CST, or at least `arbitrary_precision` plus preserved raw arrays.

### 8. MEDIUM: one version-less or dynamic-version member aborts the entire `version` run (REPRODUCED)
- **Trigger:** a Cargo member with `publish = false` and no `version` (xtask-style, which Cargo allows). A pyproject with `dynamic = ["version"]` (hatch-vcs, setuptools-scm) behaves the same.
- **Output:** E013 for the whole workspace, even though that member is not being released. The help text only suggests excluding it from discovery.
- **Location:** E013 raised from `current_version` in `crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs` and `python.rs`.
- **Fix direction:** skip non-publishable or dynamic-version members with a warning unless they are named by a changeset or edge.

### 9. MEDIUM: Python `~=` and Poetry rewrites change compatibility precision (REPRODUCED)
- **Location:** `crates/callisto-manifests/src/python.rs:772-810` (`rewrite_single`, `render_target` always emit `major.minor.patch`).
- **Trigger:** `Core[extra] ~= 1.2` with `core` going to 2.0.0.
- **Output:** the spec becomes `Core[extra]~=2.0.0`. That is narrower: `~=1.2` allowed 1.x, `~=2.0.0` allows only 2.0.x. A consumer wanting core 2.1 hits a resolver conflict. Cargo and npm keep precision; PEP 440 does not.
- **Fix direction:** keep the original component count for `~=`.

### 10. LOW-MEDIUM: Poetry dependency rewrites drop trailing comments (REPRODUCED)
- **Location:** `crates/callisto-manifests/src/python.rs:600` (`fields.insert("version", value(...))`) and `:603` (`table.insert(name, ...)`). Neither carries over decor, unlike `cargo::set_dependency_version`.
- **Trigger:** `core = "^1.2"  # keep poetry`, and `version = "~1.2.3"  # c2` under `[tool.poetry.dependencies.core]`.
- **Output:** both comments are lost. PEP 621 arrays keep theirs via `Array::replace`. The doc comment on `PyprojectToml` claims "100% CST comment preservation".
- **Fix direction:** copy `decor()` as `set_scalar_preserving_decor` does.

### 11. LOW-MEDIUM: apply is not transactional, and preflight does not dry-run the edits (REPRODUCED)
- **Location:** `crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs` (write loop) and `crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs:560-575` (`write_version` needs `package` to be a block table).
- **Trigger:** `a` (normal) and `b` with `package = { name = "b", version = "1.0.0" }`, both named in one changeset.
- **Output:** `a/Cargo.toml` is already rewritten to 1.1.0 when `b` fails with E013. Nothing is staged. The next run then hits E121 because the tree differs from HEAD.
- **Related:** the same shape applies to an E208 lockfile-refresh failure after writes. That one is documented in `docs/architecture/versioning.md`.
- **Fix direction:** open every manifest and apply all mutations in memory before the first persist (a two-phase apply).

### 12. LOW: snapshot tag validation (REPRODUCED)
- **Trigger:** `snapshot --tag feat/x_y`, `a b`, `..` or `é`.
- **Output:** E038 "internal error computing bumped version" instead of a usage error. `--tag x+y` is accepted for SemVer as `0.0.0-x+y-<sha>`, which puts the sha in build metadata. Two snapshots with the same tag then compare equal.
- **Fix direction:** validate the tag up front against the native grammar and map it to a user-facing diagnostic.

## Smaller notes (not ranked)
- A changeset naming `core` and `cargo/core` produces a duplicated changelog bullet. The max severity is correct.
- Blank continuation lines in changelog bullets carry two trailing spaces (`render.rs` `replace('\n', "\n  ")`).
- A pnpm `catalog:` spec is never rewritten, and an unmatched catalog entry is only warned about. This is by spec, but a major bump leaves the catalog pinned to the old major.
- Dead path: `VersionWriteTarget::CargoWorkspacePackage` is never produced by the planner (only tests), so `[workspace.package] version` is never written. A member with `version.workspace = true` is pinned to a literal on bump, which looks intended.

## Done well
- **Cargo.toml edits:** the CST edits preserve comments, inline tables, dotted keys (`core.version = ...`), renamed `package =` deps, target-specific and build/dev tables, and CRLF and BOM on members. Duplicate keys are rejected on parse.
- **Cargo workspace inheritance:** `workspace = true` deps are rewritten once in the root `[workspace.dependencies]`, including when the root is itself a package (r15).
- **Cascade:** it converged on peer cycles, with escalation and fixed-group handling (r7). A rewrite that would still exclude the new version is declined rather than written, and bare-caret coverage of `0.x` and prereleases is correct. Pre-mode lifecycle worked end to end: `beta.0`, `beta.1`, `pre exit` stabilises dependents, and floors are raised (r6).
- **Write primitive:** `callisto_model::atomic_write` fsyncs the file and the parent, keeps the file mode, and is gated by `ApplyPermit`. The `check_partial_run` E121 guard stops stacked double bumps after an interrupted run. The per-file `from`/`to` precondition (`write_version_guarded`) makes replay safe.
- **Changeset parser:** strict and well-specified. It handles BOM, CRLF and CR, quoted names containing `:`, duplicate detection with line numbers, and an empty summary rejection. Hostile summaries (`---`, headings, HTML) are indented into a bullet and cannot create a top-level changelog heading.
